result.title: Offline Approximate Value Iteration: A Reinforcement Learning Approach for Satellite Constellation Deployment
result.summary: This paper introduces a reinforcement learning-based approximate dynamic programming approach to optimize the deployment of Walker-type satellite constellations under uncertainties, including launch failures and satellite malfunctions. We formulate the problem as a Markov Decision Process that incorporates low-injection orbit launches, continuous low-thrust orbit raising, and variable satellite loads. We adopt the offline approximate value iteration solution method, using linear function approximation with basis functions and action pruning strategies to substantially reduce the computational and memory requirements for finding optimal decision policies. Preliminary results demonstrate convergence to policies with low expected costs and deployment times, both of which are lower than those of a rolling-horizon baseline, showcasing a novel application of approximate dynamic programming in space logistics.

AI.brief_summary: 将 Walker 型卫星星座在发射失败、卫星故障等不确定性下的部署问题建模为 MDP，采用带线性函数逼近与动作剪枝的离线近似值迭代求解策略，并与滚动时域基线比较预期成本与部署时间。
AI.relevance_reason: 近似值迭代与动作剪枝用值函数和剪枝压缩搜索与计算，可能为 LVR 中的价值式停止决策与推理步数/计算分配提供类比线索，但领域距离较远，需核查其剪枝准则是否可迁移。
